title: Geometric-stalk single-complex base-change comparison
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, $f':X'\to Y'$ be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use the small-model unbounded derived tensor pullbacks and flat-term K-flat coefficient-map coordinates [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback-models], with the normalized geometric stalks and pullback-stalk isomorphisms [def-sfb-space-geometric-stalk-models]. For a geometric $x':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X'$, put $x=g'x'$, $y'=f'x'$, $y=fx$, and $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y',y'}$, $C=\mathcal O_{X',x'}$. Transport the $R$-algebra structure on $B$ along the square equation, and let $A\otimes_R B\to C$ be the unique ring map restricting to the two projection stalk maps. For $\phi:L(g')^*K\to K'$ define $\beta^i_{\phi,x'}:H^i(K_x\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_{A\otimes_R B}C\to H^i(K'_{x'})$ by the existing canonical base-derived tensor cohomology model [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model], followed by the normalized pullback-stalk identification and the stalk of the chain representative of $\phi$. Define the stalk condition to mean that this map is invertible for every geometric point, every integer degree, and every such coordinate presentation. The derived-counit equation ensures that all these presentations describe the same canonical map. The coordinate presentations exist; no boundedness or square flatness is imposed.
